title: Natural Calamities & Disaster Management Flashcards
description: Key facts from TNPSC Group II Geography Disaster Management Chapter

cards.q: From which French word is the term 'Disaster' derived, and what does it mean?
What are the two broad categories of disasters?
cards.a: Natural Disasters (earthquakes, floods, cyclones, etc.) and Man-Made Disasters (industrial/chemical accidents, nuclear accidents, etc.).

cards.q: Which coast of India is more vulnerable to cyclones - Eastern or Western?
cards.a: The Eastern Coast (Bay of Bengal) is more cyclone-prone than the Western Coast (Arabian Sea).

cards.q: What are the three types of drought?
cards.a: Meteorological Drought, Hydrological Drought, and Agricultural Drought.

cards.q: What rooftop method is recommended for drought mitigation to retain water for various uses?
When did the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami occur and how many lives were lost?
cards.a: 26th December 2004; more than 3,00,000 lives were lost.

cards.q: Which international system did India join after the 2004 Tsunami disaster?
When did the Bhopal Gas Tragedy occur and which gas was leaked?
cards.a: 3rd December 1984; Methyl Isocyanate (MIC) gas leaked from the Union Carbide plant.

cards.q: What are the four main phases of Disaster Management?
Who heads the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)?
Who heads the State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA)?
Who heads the District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA)?
Who heads the National Executive Committee (NEC) for disaster management?
Who heads the State Executive Committee (SEC) for disaster management?
In which year was the Disaster Management Act enacted?
In which year was the National Policy on Disaster Management formulated?
What does FACT stand for in the context of the IFRC's disaster response?
What does IEC stand for in the context of disaster awareness?
What specialized force has been established in India for disaster response?
Name two key afforestation-related drought mitigation measures mentioned in the text.
cards.a: 1. Afforestation to retain humidity and promote precipitation. 2. Ban on cutting of trees and clearing of forests.
